requirement: JWT validation utility strictly enforcing expiration ('exp') claims, requiring mandatory 'exp' presence, limiting clock skew leeway to safe boundaries (<= 30s), and rejecting expired tokens.
skeleton: ExpirableTokenManager class with issue_token and decode_token methods using PyJWT.

rationale.teaches: JWT decoding that requires exp and iat, verifies expiry, caps leeway at 30 seconds, raises on an expired token, and issues tokens that expire in the future.
rationale.why: An expired token has a valid signature, so only the exp check rejects it. The fixture issues a token with a past exp and expects a ValueError, and checks the leeway boundary.

candidates.why_wrong: verify_exp is off, so an expired token is accepted.
exp is not required, so a token that never expires is accepted.
Leeway has no upper bound, so a caller can set an hour of leeway and accept long-expired tokens.
An expired token is returned with an is_expired flag, so callers who ignore the flag accept it.
exp is set to now minus ttl, so every issued token is already expired.
